newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Transport Ministry proposes floating El Al.
newsitem.headline: Israel Transport Ministry proposes floating El Al.

text.p: Israel's Transport Ministry has prepared a plan to float the government's entire shareholding in state-owned El Al airlines in the domestic market, a ministry spokesman said on Thursday.

"The plan for the sale of all the shares of El Al to the public will be presented next week to officials in the prime minister's office," the spokesman said. "We're aiming to implement the sale during 1997."
He said the ministry was proposing to float the shares without underwriters and that an undetermined percentage would be offered to the airline's employees.

Under the terms of the proposal, no single shareholder could hold more than five percent of El Al in the first year after the offering, the spokesman said. The government currently controls 100 percent of the carrier.

El Al is not among the companies included in the government's privatisation plan for 1997. The airline, which has been profitable for most of the last decade, is expected to post a huge loss for 1996.
El Al has estimated its losses could reach $100 million for 1996. Newspaper reports have said the company aims to trim the loss to $20 million from $40 million this year.

Privatisation has also been dogged by concerns that a ban on flights on the Jewish Sabbath and holidays as well as heavy security costs would discourage investors. A committee headed by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's economics adviser Moshe Leon was due to have completed an investigation of these issues by mid-January.

The spokesman said Transport Minister Yitzhak Levy would make El Al's privatisation conditional on continuing the ban on Sabbath flights. But Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said last month the Sabbath flight issue had not yet been decided.
The government's last effort at floating El Al, in a global offering, was cut short when underwriters assigned the carrier what the Treasury considered very low valuations of $90 to $150 million.
